# LoopDuet: Not All Loops Cost the Same: Phase-Dependent Depth for Serving Looped Transformers

English · [简体中文](../zh/2611.07211.md) · [Back to the list](../../README.md)

<sub>arXiv 2611.07211 · 2026-11-04 · Duke University</sub>

<img src="../../assets/glyphs/2611.07211.svg" alt="prelude 4 layers -&gt; [core 6 layers] x 32 (OLMo r32 checkpoint) -&gt; coda 4 layers; injection n/a; KV last-pass">

> Serve looped Transformers with fewer core loops for ordinary prompt tokens than for the last prompt token and the decoded tokens, run the deep tail as a compact batch in vLLM, and lower prefilling depth when the queue grows.

**Category**: Systems and inference · **Status**: draft (numbers not yet re-checked) · **Impact**: cites 1

[paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07211)

## Problem

Serving a looped model with one loop count for all tokens ties prefill cost to decode depth. With long prompts and short answers (OLMo HotpotQA prompts average 796 tokens and answers about 4.7), prompt positions account for over 99% of layer applications, so keeping deep decoding repeats deep computation over the whole prompt.

## Method

- Choose decode depth S and prefill depth P <= S jointly from measured quality-throughput trade-offs; ordinary prompt positions stop after P core loops, while every prompt-chunk endpoint and every decoded token runs S.
- In vLLM, after P loops the engine gathers each request's final query into a compact B x d batch for the remaining S - P loops and scatters it back before the coda; prompt context stays in one shared KV plane per core layer, so existing weights and attention kernels are reused.
- A queue-age controller maps the oldest first-token wait from 0.25 s to 1 s linearly onto [P_min, P_max] before each engine step, keeping S fixed (main setting S = 4, P in {2, 3, 4}).
- A recurrent-state distance (90th percentile over ordinary prompt tokens, threshold about 0.24) screens candidate P values before task-accuracy checks.

## Loop layout

| Facet | Value |
|---|---|
| Where the loop sits | middle core (prelude-core-coda) |
| Weight sharing | fully tied |
| Passes in training | n/a |
| Passes at test time | adaptive exit / routing |
| Input injection | n/a |
| KV cache | last-pass KV only |
| Gradient through passes | n/a |
| Origin | n/a |
| FFN | dense FFN |
| Attention in the loop | full attention |
| Passes (R6) | train 32 (OLMo r32 checkpoint); test S for decode, P <= S for prefill, at most 32 |

Shown for OLMo r32, a recurrent OLMo-2 retrofit with 4/6/4 prelude/core/coda layers at width 2,048 (the r16 checkpoint has the same layout and was trained at 16 loops); Huginn-0125 has 2/4/2 layers at width 5,280. LoopDuet trains nothing. Ordinary prompt positions run P core loops, while every prompt-chunk endpoint and every decoded token runs S. Serving keeps one shared KV plane per core layer that each loop overwrites, so later queries read the last computed KV of positions that stopped early.

## Other findings

- The first output token needs full depth: for Huginn on HotpotQA at S = 32 with other prompt positions at P = 16, running the final prompt position at 16 loops instead of 32 lowers EM by 1.74 points relative to (32, 16) and by 1.97 points relative to (32, 32). (Section 4.5)
- Split budgets do not always win: Huginn (24, 12) gives 31.60 EM at 2.43 req/s, while uniform (12, 12) gives 32.05 EM at 2.48 req/s. (Section 4.2; Table 1)
- For OLMo r32 on HotpotQA, EM stays between 37.95 and 38.49 across all six tested settings, so uniform depth four, the fastest at 56.46 req/s and 0.54 points below (32, 32), is chosen as the controller's starting point. (Section 4.2; Figure A1; Table A6)
- Useful prefilling depth is task dependent: on ARC at S = 11, raising OLMo r32's P from 4 to 8 moves the accuracy change from -1.54 to +0.85 points, and Huginn (14, 8) stays 4.44 points below (14, 14). (Section 4.5; Figure 8)
- The savings survive batching: Huginn (32, 16) keeps 1.84x, 1.87x and 1.88x speedups over (32, 32) at engine-step token budgets of 4,096, 8,192 and 16,384 (C = 128), and 1.87x at C = 32, 64 and 128. (Section 4.3; Table A9)

## Comparison

- **Baseline**: Uniform-depth serving (S, S) of the same checkpoint in the same vLLM engine, with the same prompts, KV layout, precision and execution mode; (32, 32) is the full-depth reference, and fixed prefilling depths at the same S are the controls under load.
- **Held fixed**: N (unique parameters), D (training tokens), KV (KV cache per token)
- **Differs**: L (executed layers per token), W (wall-clock time)
- **Baseline hyperparameters**: shared with the looped model
- **Headline claim**: On full HotpotQA with one A100-80GB, Huginn (32, 16) gives 1.19x the throughput of (20, 20), the fastest tested uniform setting meeting the same accuracy criterion, and (14, 8) gains 6.04 EM points over uniform (8, 8) at 97% of its throughput. Under load, adapting OLMo's prefilling depth gains 0.92-1.35 EM points over the most accurate tested fixed depths at the same 100% one-second TTFT attainment. (Abstract; Figure 3; Table 1; Table 2)

## Caveats

- Training-free serving study of existing checkpoints only (Huginn-0125 and the recurrent OLMo-2 retrofits r16 and r32); every tested depth is at most 32 loops (16 for OLMo r16).
- Tasks are GSM8K, HotpotQA (distractor dev set) and ARC-Challenge, with model-specific prompts (OLMo four paragraphs and one demonstration under a 1,000-token cap; Huginn ten paragraphs and two demonstrations); the authors call these within-model comparisons, not a ranking between models.
- All timings use one A100-SXM4-80GB, vLLM 0.14.1, bf16 and no prefix caching; the joint-depth comparison uses one execution per configuration at C = 64.
- Gains depend on the workload: on GSM8K, longer responses give wall-time ratios of 0.98-1.01 across four serving pairs despite layer-pass ratios of 1.52-2.71.
- Decoding reads prompt KV from the last loop each position computed, an approximation to full-depth context that the authors evaluate through task accuracy; the controller has no correctness feedback and works within a depth range chosen offline.
- On the 20/80 req/s burst trace the controller reaches 87.5% one-second TTFT attainment, against 100% for fixed P = 2.
